guest.bio_context: Zach Holman joined GitHub in 2010 and spent five years there before the company was acquired by Microsoft in 2017. After GitHub, he moved into advising companies including GitLab, which led him to angel investing — an activity he has been doing for seven to eight years. He has invested in approximately a couple hundred companies across sectors including developer tools and sports, and built Signed.com out of his own frustration with spreadsheet-based portfolio tracking.

pending_qa.q: What is Zach Holman's approach to investing in sports teams as an angel investor?
pending_qa.r: Zach Holman has invested in Oakland Roots SC by cold-DMing the club's chairman and joining as an investor, has joined the ownership group of Cagliari in Serie A Italy at the end of last year, and has invested in a fund that acquires European women's league clubs. He views sports investing similarly to angel investing — backing things he is personally interested in, even when the financial logic would not satisfy traditional fund LPs.

pending_qa.q: How is Signed.com priced and what are its tiers?
pending_qa.r: Signed.com offers a free tier for investors with a small number of investments, an angel-level tier, and a higher institutional tier. Pricing is based on features rather than the dollar amount invested, a decision Holman made after realizing that gating by investment size discouraged users from entering accurate on-paper valuations — particularly founder equity — because they did not want to trigger higher fees.

pending_qa.q: What is QSBS treatment and how does Signed.com address it?
pending_qa.r: QSBS (Qualified Small Business Stock) is a tax treatment relevant to angel investors that affects how returns are taxed, and it interacts with other account types such as Roth IRAs where returns are calculated differently than in taxable accounts. Signed.com is building functionality to help investors track QSBS eligibility alongside other tax-related details, so investors have a cleaner picture of their after-tax returns across different account types.

pending_qa.q: Can Signed.com be used to track investments made through equity crowdfunding platforms like WeFunder?
pending_qa.r: Yes — Zach Holman himself invested in Oakland Roots SC through WeFunder, which created a separate SPV to accommodate the roughly four to five thousand investors in that crowdfunding campaign, resulting in K-1 issuance. Signed.com is designed to handle these kinds of investments, including tracking K-1 sources and helping investors understand why their K-1 figures may differ year over year due to liquidity events or write-offs within the fund.
